lecture: From a model to a solved assignment

bilingual.title: From acceleration to velocity
terms: At the start; v0 is velocity at time zero.
Change in graph height divided by change in time.

notes.label: Prerequisite bridge
notes.text: A subscript identifies a particular value. The 0 in v0 labels the start; it does not multiply v. Acceleration of 3 m/s2 adds 3 m/s of velocity each second.

homework.label: Homework connection
homework.text: For part (a), first calculate the gain a t = 12 m/s, then add the starting 2 m/s. The endpoint 14 m/s also feeds the graph check in part (c).
homework.source: Full authored question and guided solution: study-guide pages 6-7.

bilingual.title: Displacement is the area under velocity
terms: Final position minus starting position; it is signed.
The constant velocity producing the same displacement.
A four-sided region with one pair of parallel sides.

notes.label: Why this relation follows
notes.text: Velocity times a short time interval gives a small displacement. Add these strips to get the area. Since the velocity line is straight, its average height is halfway between the endpoint heights.

homework.label: Homework connection
homework.text: Part (c) splits the shaded region into an 8 m rectangle and a 24 m triangle. Their sum checks part (b). Distance equals forward displacement here because the cart does not reverse.
homework.source: Original authored graph; study-guide pages 3 and 7.

bilingual.title: Build the constant-acceleration equation
terms: Replace a quantity with an expression equal to it.
Multiply every term inside a sum by the outside factor.
The physical kind of a quantity, such as length or time.

notes.label: The new notation and the one-half
notes.text: Delta x is change in position; t squared is time multiplied by itself. The one-half comes from the triangular extra area, not from an arbitrary instruction to divide the final answer.

homework.label: Homework connection
homework.text: Part (b) separates starting-motion displacement, 8 m, from acceleration's extra 24 m. Both terms must have units of metres. The new practice on page 8 checks whether the reasoning transfers.
